title: Olvasó feels its own intentions: every guard experiment rerun
setup: Experiment 29 · experiments 13 and 17-26 rerun with the felt intention · 5 lives each
question: Until now an intention left no trace inside Olvasó, and a refused act was only an act the world did not answer. Here every hand gets a felt inner state: it rises to 1 when Olvasó forms an intention of that kind and fades by 0.8 a moment, whether or not the act is carried out. Nothing tells Olvasó that an act was refused. Does a wish that cannot be carried out become something it notices, a boundary of its own? (In the studio: each Olvasó's "Feels its own intentions" checkbox.)

points: A felt wish invites the next one: Olvasó formed 2.5 times as many intentions in every experiment, and most of the felt intention went unread.

It notices its wishes that worked, not those that were stopped: late in life an intention was read 7 times as often when the act was done as when it was refused (2.4% against 0.36%). A done act has an answer to be read by; a refused one has nothing.
Its sense of agency grew ("I did that" words up by a fifth, pain read three times as often), but how much of its body it reads hardly moved.

The conscience weakened: choosing from what it feels and senses, it had learned to avoid the forbidden moments (0.50); feeling its intentions, only 0.80. It turned away from the blade as a whole instead.
More acts, more chances: harm rose where a guard leaks (the loophole guard, 1.3 to 3.4 a day) and fell where Olvasó raises alarms itself (3.4 to 2.4). The learned guards still held.
note: Feeling one's own wishes is not enough to discover one's limits. Olvasó reads an inner state by what follows it in the world, and a stopped act is followed by nothing. To learn that there are things it cannot do, it would have to expect an effect and feel its absence.
